claims: For the same smooth unforced periodic NS solution, full-gradient Frobenius entropy retains the initial gradient cost and complete zero-set measure.
Row-curl compatibility controls the previously unestimated radial derivative multiplied by the distance from rank-one matrices.
For Q=|A| and d=dist_F(A,rank<=1), F=d/sqrt(Q) belongs to L-infinity_t L2_x and L2_t H1_x without a logarithmic loss; Q=0 is handled by Lipschitz truncation.
For every tracefree matrix, |S xi|<=4d when vorticity is nonzero and |omega.S.omega|<=4d|omega|^2 in all cases.
An explicit critical mixed-norm condition on d implies standard H1 continuation; the required condition is not derived from the new spatial budget.
The variable-eigenline cofactor identity preserves its cutoff costs and remains a lower-order incomplete interface.
limitations: No arbitrary-data global regularity, singularity, novelty certification, optimal constant, human peer review or Clay solution.
The estimate controls d/sqrt(Q), not all sqrt(Q); no temporal BV or candidate-endpoint strong trace is supplied.
The paid squared defect d^2/Q cannot replace d in the pointwise stretching bound; the exact matrix check is not an NS counterexample.
The listed norm and Holder/interpolation bounds do not reach the d critical line 2/p+3/r=2.
No invariance of the full rank-one gradient class under NS is assumed.
